newsitem.title: USA: Kubo explains rules on Japan insurance niche mkts.
newsitem.headline: Kubo explains rules on Japan insurance niche mkts.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Tuesday that domestic insurance subsidiaries will not be barred from selling all products in the niche market where foreign firms have a strong foothold.

In his last news conference before leaving Washington for Tokyo, Kubo released a translated extract of the memorandam which said that the subsidiaries of life insurance firms will be blocked from offering personal insurance policies until January 1, 1997.
Meanwhile, subsidiaries of Japanese non-life insurance firms will be barred from selling stand-alone cancer, hospitalisation and nusring care insurance policies, it said.
Asked whether these were the only products Japanese insurance units were barred from in the so-called "third sector" niche market, Kubo said: "Yes, that's it."

Kubo was responding to questions about comments made by Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky earlier Tuesday. She said the subsidiaries will be barred from the thrid sector entry until a comprehensive agreement is reached.
Japan and U.S. agreed on Monday to reach a final decision by December 15 over a long-simmering bilateral dispute as to how to open up Japan's $382 billion insurance market.

He added that if Japan and the U.S. fail to settle the dispute, domestic insurance units will be allowed to sell all products in the third sector from January 1 under the current conditions issued to the insurance companies.
However, the conditions put on insurance subsidiares may be altered if both Japan and the U.S. agree on the changes, he added.

Kubo was in Washington from Saturday to attend the Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central governors meeting as well as the annual meeting of International Monetary Fund and World Bank. During his stay, he met with Barshefsky over dinner on Sunday to discuss bilateral insurance dispute.
